label: copy-phase input v, esp. when next output is v/i/m/x/d
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase on steps whose input is the fed-back token v (99.97% of activations have in_tok=v; never in the original or delimiter phases, never on any other input). Only ~10% of copy-phase v inputs activate, though. Whether it fires depends on the token being output at that step: strongest when out_tok is v again (a repeated v, e.g. top example v m v v <DEL> v m [v]; 74% precision), then i, m, x, d. It is also stronger later in the copy (recall_idx >= 3, near the end of the sequence) and weak or absent at recall_idx 1. The largest activations are short sequences (L=4) ending in v v, at the step where the first v is fed back and the second v is output. It is mostly silent on copy-phase v inputs followed by other outputs. The predicate gets about 0.54 precision / 0.71 recall / 0.84 mass recall on dev.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=9: v, i; t=8: v; t=7: v) and the token being output (most: v, m, i, x, d, h; least: p, f, g, z); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=4, L=4 & t=5, recall_idx=4.
